discernment_questions: Does declining come with any implied or explicit cost, or is "no" treated as a complete, respected answer?
Is pressure, guilt, or a sense of owing invoked to override a decline?
Does this happen as a pattern, or was this a single, honest expression of disappointment that still respected the answer?
Would consent given here be genuinely free, or given specifically to avoid a consequence?
less_concerning_if: A "no" is fully respected without any implied cost, even alongside honest disappointment.
more_concerning_if: Declining carries implied or explicit consequences, and pressure or guilt is used to override the answer.
existing_specific_text.repair_check: After the incident, was there a genuine acknowledgment (not a non-apology), a concrete change in behavior, and no repeat of the same pattern? Repair is a pattern of change over time, not a single sentence of regret.
existing_specific_text.boundary_respect_check: When a boundary was stated plainly in this area, was it honored going forward — or tested, ignored, punished, or reframed as unreasonable? Boundary respect observed over multiple instances is one of the more reliable signals available.
existing_specific_text.psychological_mechanism: One documented mechanism behind patterns like this is that they can operate by compressing the time or space available to think, so a decision gets made under urgency instead of consideration. This describes a possible mechanism, not a claim about what any specific person intended.
existing_specific_text.possible_impact_on_receiver: People sometimes describe decision fatigue and a pattern of agreeing to things in the moment that don't hold up on reflection in connection with patterns like this. Impact varies widely by person, history, and context — this is a possibility to consider, not a predicted or universal outcome, and it is not a diagnosis of the person on the receiving end of a sustained pattern like this.
existing_specific_text.boundary_script: Given the safety dimension of this category, a scripted line matters less than the surrounding plan: if and when it feels safe, a simple, low-detail line like "I need some space and I'll reach out when I'm ready" is enough — it does not require justification. See the Safety note below before deciding how, when, or whether to address this directly with the person involved.
existing_specific_text.safety_note: A phrase-matching tool cannot decide safety. If this involves threats, monitoring, isolation, sex, money, housing, immigration, self-harm pressure, retaliation, or fear for safety, prioritize real-world support from a trusted person, local support service, legal/workplace resource, or emergency help if immediate danger exists.
misuse_warning: One example is a signal to examine, not proof of motive, diagnosis, abuse, danger, or character. Do not use this label to attack, shame, threaten, expose, or retaliate against someone.

related_tactics.name: Ultimatums
related_tactics.definition: Forcing a binary choice under threat of loss.

related_tactics.name: Urgency Manufacturing
related_tactics.definition: Compressing time so the target can't think or consult.

related_tactics.name: False Dilemma
related_tactics.definition: Presenting two options when more exist.

related_tactics.name: Sunk Cost Exploitation
related_tactics.definition: Using past investment to block present exit.

related_tactics.name: Response-Time Policing
related_tactics.definition: Treating reply latency as an offense requiring explanation.

related_tactics.name: Interrogation
related_tactics.definition: Demanding justification as an entitlement, on command.

old_safety_signals.note: Old signals were set by a coarse rule. Decide safety_sensitive yourself from the spec; these are hints only.
